target: Messier 27 (NGC 6853), the Dumbbell Nebula, a planetary nebula in Vulpecula
reproduce: hack/stacks/2026-10-17/m27/run_all.sh (hooks M27_*, see common.py); with none set it reproduces this run. RAWs ~/.observatory/stills/2026-10-18/ read in place, never written
template: hack/stacks/2026-10-12/m77-calibrated (calibrated flat, Gaia star colours, darks.subtract) with the combine of hack/stacks/2026-10-12/ngc891-coadd (proper coaddition, keep_phase="mean"; the old sigma-clipped weighted mean made from the same cube as a control, work/control_*.npy)

summary.frames: 70 taken in the run (15 s, ISO 3200 by the RAW's own EXIF; every one plate-solved on M27 by its sidecar); 66 used, 4 dropped

summary.not_in_the_run: before 03:46 UTC: centring frames (2 s at ISO 6400, a 1/60 s frame) and the focusing frames on Vega (2 s, 03:06 to 03:25); from 04:23 UTC, M33 (another target, used only for a candidate flat). None of these is in the stack
summary.transparency: 0.980 to 1.009 of the run's typical star flux: no cloud
summary.star_size: half-flux diameter, green, 117 compact unsaturated stars: 4.47 arcsec in the stack, 4.94 in the reference frame alone; the run's frames 4.64 (median, step 4). The box's own figure (the 960 px JPEG preview) read 6.2 to 7.3 arcsec for the same frames: a coarser measure of the same stars
summary.flat: the 13 October hybrid flat (~/.observatory/nights/2026-10-12-a6000/flat-hybrid-m77: large scale from that night's open sky of NGC 891, NGC 2261, NGC 2419 and M1; dust from the 13 October twilight flats), chosen over two others on this run's own sky (step 7a), times this run's own measure of the dust that moved since (step 7)
summary.dust: three shadows named for tonight, their depth in this run's own sky before any flat / after the 13 October flat / after this run's own correction: crescent at sensor (3534, 824): 12.7% / 12.6% / 1.7%; spot_a at sensor (1356, 2400): 5.5% / 0.5% / 0.1%; spot_b at sensor (5352, 3456): 9.0% / 0.2% / 0.2%. The crescent is new since 13 October (the twilight flat has only a 3% shadow there) and is taken out by this run's own measure; the two spots were already in the 13 October flat. 11 shadows in all were measured on this run's sky (seen in the odd and in the even frames alone) and divided out, 0.73% of the sensor
summary.darks: none taken tonight: darks.subtract changed nothing and said so; hot pixels found from the run itself and repaired by the 3 x 3 median of their colour plane
summary.combine: proper coaddition (Zackay & Ofek 2017; tools/coadd.py, keep_phase="mean"), 269 PSF stars per plane, one PSF per frame and plane; theory S/N gain over the old weighted mean 1.0100 (green). The old combine is made from the same cube as a control
summary.noise: sky noise per stack pixel 6.2 to 8.2 DN against 48.1 to 60.8 for one frame: 7.45 to 7.75 times lower (8.12 expected from the weights)
summary.is_it_the_thing: yes: the reference frame and the stack plate-solved (astrometry.net); M27's central star's catalogue place falls 0.7 arcsec from the light's centroid in the stack
summary.ears: the faint outer lobes ("ears", filling the nebula out along its long axis, position angle about 90 to 150 and 270 to 330 degrees) are real: 3 to 4 arcmin from the star they are 12/12, 11/11, 6/6, 4/4, 12/12, 12/12, 5/5 sigma above blank sky in the odd and in the even frames alone (step 12). Beyond 4 arcmin no sector passes in either half: the faint outer halo seen in deep pictures (out to about 7 arcmin) is NOT seen in 16.5 minutes from this sky
summary.followed: the nebula followed (ring median of green above 3 x the blank-sky spread, unbroken from the star) to 4.04 arcmin from the star, 8.1 arcmin across
summary.colour: the camera's daylight white balance times Gaia DR3 star colours (kR 1.0128, kB 1.1530 from 93 stars), the camera's own colour matrix. The nebula's blue-green (doubly ionised oxygen, 501 nm) is outside sRGB; colour shown only above 8 DN, grey below. No saturation beyond x 1.2
summary.picture: a 1200 x 1000 px cut at the stack's own pixels (0.777 arcsec per px, 15.5 x 12.9 arcmin), nothing resampled after the stack, never enlarged; north 116.2 degrees clockwise from up (the camera's orientation)

steps.step: 6 is it the thing (reference frame plate solve)
7a candidate flats on this run's own sky (flatcheck.py)
steps.said: hybrid13 leaves the least on this sky after a plane (green 0.57%, against 0.80% for the M33 flat and 1.98% for the twilight flat as measured). M33 is bigger than the frame, so its run is not open sky; its flat is kept as a candidate only. Every flat leaves this run's dust about 70% as deep as it carries it (correlation 0.35): the dust moved since 13 October, so step 7 measures it here

steps.step: 7 flat check and this run's own dust

flat_from.made_from: the night's own open sky (ngc891, ngc2261, ngc2419, m1) for the large scale; twilight flats (/Users/bradgessler/.observatory/nights/2026-10-12-a6000/flat-twilight) for dust and pixel response
flat_from.formula: flat[p] = large[p] x twilight small scale[p], 1 at the sensor centre; divide plane p (black subtracted) by it

dust.what: this run's own green sky over the flat, over its own 160 px scale, Gaussian 1 block (8 px): a shadow the flat left is where that is below 1 - 0.012 over at least 6 blocks and at least 0.006 deep in the even and in the odd frames alone. There the flat is multiplied by the measured remainder (bilinear from the blocks, never above 1); it is the night's flat everywhere else. The same factor for all four colours.
dust.why: the night's flat left every one of its own shadows 1 to 5% deep under this run's sky (it carries them shallower than they are here)
dust.blind: within 390 plane px (5.0 arcmin) of the nucleus, in every frame's own place, no dust can be judged from these frames (the galaxy's bright middle)

air_dispersion.how: red and blue sampled at green's place plus their offset, in the one Lanczos-4 resampling

R.paper: Zackay B. & Ofek E. O. 2017, ApJ 836, 188 (arXiv:1512.06879)
R.tool: coadd.py 1.1 (2026-10-17): mean PSF phase kept, measured outlier thresholds, two-pass refill
R.formula: R_hat = sum_j (F_j/s_j^2) conj(P_hat_j) M_hat_j / sqrt(sum_j (F_j^2/s_j^2) |P_hat_j|^2); S = R / F_R, F_R = sqrt(sum_j F_j^2/s_j^2); PSF of S: P_R_hat = sqrt(sum_j (F_j^2/s_j^2) |P_hat_j|^2) / F_R
R.linear: given the outlier mask, S is linear in the frames; the weights and filters come from the PSFs and the noise only

outliers.rule: flag |X_j - m| > kappa sqrt(r_j^2 + (beta m)^2) per pixel, or |B(X_j - m)| > kappa_smooth sqrt(b_j^2 + (beta B(m))^2) with B a 3 x 3 box mean; grow 1 px; X_j = frame / F_j, m the per-pixel median of all frames that have the pixel, r_j and b_j the robust (1.4826 MAD) spread of X_j - m and of B(X_j - m) over the frame, times noise_map
outliers.beta_why: from the PSFs: the largest peak ratio to the median is 1.292; beta = max(0.50, 2 x 0.292 / kappa)

target.target: mean-psf: |sum_j w_j P_hat_j| / sum_j w_j, w_j = F_j^2 / s_j^2 (a weighted mean's PSF, its phase dropped)

field_variation.rule: varies if the zones differ by > 3 x the halves' noise and by > 3% in HFD or > 0.05 in ellipticity

to_common.target: the minimum of the full set's and both halves' P_R_hat, with the full set's phase

steps.step: 9 plate solve of the stack and the crop

galaxy_crop.why: the field is 39 x 26 arcmin and the nebula's bright body 8 x 5.6 inside a halo about 15 across: a 1200 x 1000 px cut around the central star's catalogue place at the stack's own pixels (15.5 x 12.9 arcmin), nothing resampled

numbers.north_in_words: north is 116.2 degrees clockwise from up (east 26.2): in the picture north points to the lower right; the sky as seen, not mirrored

sun_like_stars.rule: BP - RP 0.72 to 0.92, linear sRGB through the camera matrix; white is 1, 1

colour_term.per: mag of residual per mag of BP - RP, all measured stars 0.3 to 2.0 not clipped

radial_term.per: mag of residual per 1000 sensor px from the sensor centre (stars of the fit)

catalogue.name: Gaia DR3
catalogue.epoch: positions at 2016.0 (ICRS); move them with the proper motions to the night

numbers.reference_white: the Sun's colour (Gaia BP - RP 0.82) is white
numbers.model: BP - RP -> T (Mucciarelli & Bellazzini 2020, dwarfs) -> black body -> CIE 1931 (Wyman et al. 2013 fits) -> linear sRGB; measured: camera RGB x (kR, 1, kB) -> render.py camera matrix -> linear sRGB

aperture.ceiling_rule: peak / wb + sky (RAW DN) under 60% of 15488

input.what: step 8 stack_mean planes cut to step 9's rectangle (x 96..2944, y 62..1940 of the reference grid); camera R, mean of G1 and G2, B, times the daylight balance; sky at zero
input.nebula_left_out: the catalogue ellipse of step 9 (the bright body, 8 x 5.6 arcmin), semi-axes x 1.3 (+30 px across)

steps.step: 10 deliver: TIF, stretch, sky plane in the picture only, measures

tif.units: DN of the 14-bit raw scale, white-balanced (R x 2.9364, B x 1.5544), per 15 s frame at the sensor centre
tif.colour: camera RGB, daylight white balance, no colour matrix

noise_faint_region.units: DN per stack pixel, 3-sigma clipped std in the faint region (step 7)

core.what: the largest black-subtracted RAW value of each colour plane within 14 px of the nucleus, in every frame of the run (15 s, ISO 3200); the ceiling is 15488 DN above black

galaxy.what: green (mean of G1 and G2), sky plane removed, the MEDIAN in rings around the nucleus (6 px wide to 60 px, 12 px wide beyond; 1 px = 0.7766 arcsec); a median, so the stars drop out, the 10th magnitude star 1.45 arcmin from the nucleus among them

blank_sky.what: the same rings laid on 4 places of blank sky in the same stack; their spread (standard deviation between the places) at each radius is what the flat and the sky leave: the floor

followed_to.rule: the ring median above 3 x the blank-sky spread, unbroken from the centre

outer_ring.where: 2.2 to 3.6 arcmin from the nucleus (the catalogue's 7.1 x 6.0 arcmin diameters)
outer_ring.rule: every ring median there above 3 x the blank-sky spread in the stack and above 2 x in the odd and in the even frames alone

crop.why: the nebula and its halo are about 8 x 10 arcmin in a 37 x 24 arcmin field of plain sky: a cut around the central star's catalogue place at the stack's own pixels, nothing resampled

steps.how: brightness changed, each pixel's colour ratios kept

steps.brightness: bilateral filter, sigma 4.0 px, 7 L units
steps.where: full below L 8, none above L 30 (brightness judged on a blurred copy)

steps.left_alone: below L 14 (fading in to L 30) and above L 93
steps.sky_without_colour: colour fades to grey below L 8 (full colour from L 18): the dark sky's colour is noise

steps.step: 12 half stacks: are the ears real?

numbers.what: Step 12: are the faint outer lobes (the "ears", the grey halo that fills the Dumbbell out to an apple shape round the
numbers.verdict: the halo (4 to 5 arcmin from the star): seen in both halves in 0 of 12 sectors; 5 to 6.5 arcmin: 0 of 12.
